item.title: White House takes down ‘Build the Wall’ game after the Tetris Company complains
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: The Trump administration's short-lived arcade game "Build the Wall" is now nowhere to be found after the Tetris Company posted that it takes "copyright infringement very seriously."

item.title: Hackers are stealing Claude tokens from subscribers
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Last month, a Claude user noticed his account was consuming tokens even though he wasn't working. Anthropic has since warned users about hackers.

item.title: Cognition hits $48B valuation, signaling investors believe AI coding is far from a winner-take-all market
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Cognition's valuation multiple is higher than Cursor's was before selling to SpaceX.

item.title: The Exploration Company nabs $450 million to challenge SpaceX
item.dc:creator: Anna Heim
item.description: The Exploration Company (TEC) has raised $450 million to build reusable spacecraft, in what it describes as “the largest-ever Series C by a European space company.”

item.title: Meta debuts its Muse AI agent. Will consumers trust it?
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Meta's new personal AI agent Muse wants access to users' email, calendars, payments, health services, and more — making the company's biggest consumer AI bet yet a major test of whether people still trust Meta with their data.

item.title: How to watch Apple’s foldable iPhone announcement
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: Apple's annual iPhone event will stream live on September 9 at 10 a.m. PDT, and we're expecting big news.

item.title: OpenAI fought dirty on career-making math problem, says NYU mathematician
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: There is a $1 million bounty for the first person providing a solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem.

item.title: Google Cloud races to catch up in the AI deployment wars with Accenture deal
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Google Cloud expands its enterprise AI push with Accenture, betting on forward-deployed engineers to drive adoption and overcome deployment bottlenecks.

item.title: Google’s revived nuclear power plant gets $1.9B loan from US government
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Google said it would bring an Iowa nuclear power plant back from the dead. Now the plant's owner is getting a $1.9 billion loan from the U.S. Energy Department.

item.title: Chrome is now shipping updates every 2 weeks as AI changes the security landscape
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Google is speeding up Chrome’s release schedule to ship security patches and new features faster.

item.title: Mistral raises €3B as sovereign AI becomes big business
item.dc:creator: Anna Heim
item.description: The French AI lab has raised €3 billion at a €21 billion valuation in a Series D round led by Samsung, Scaleup Europe, and PSG Equity.

item.title: A hacker stole $340M in a crypto heist, then returned most of it
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The latest heist is one of the largest thefts of cryptocurrency to date.

item.title: Nuclear startup Bluecore Energy raises $50M seed round, just two months after launch
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Bluecore Energy announced Tuesday an oversubscribed $50 million seed round — just months after raising a $10 million pre-seed and coming out of stealth.

item.title: Poseidon Aerospace lands $60M ahead of first pilotless test flight
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The startup is trying to rethink the economics of cargo aircraft by removing pilots from the equation entirely.

item.title: Stoke Space raises another billion to rival SpaceX at re-flying rockets
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Stoke has "completed the initial closing" of a $1B Series E round intended to help it reach orbit and prepare a new, larger rocket for operations.

item.title: Eric Wu’s newest company, out of stealth since May, is going after construction’s labor crunch
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: Eric Wu, who built and ran Opendoor before stepping away in 2022, has had his new company, NavigateAI, out of stealth since May — building AI copilots that give construction workers real-time, hands-free guidance through smartphones and Meta's AI glasses, backed by $25 million from Elad Gil, Khosla Ventures, and Lennar to tackle a labor shortage severe enough that data center projects alone now need 4,000 to 5,000 workers apiece.

item.title: Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know
item.dc:creator: Natasha Lomas, Romain Dillet, Kyle Wiggers, Lucas Ropek
item.description: The rise of AI has brought an avalanche of new terms and slang. Here is a glossary with definitions of some of the most important words and phrases you might encounter.

item.title: A secret new Elizabeth Holmes documentary stuns Telluride
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's secret Elizabeth Holmes documentary, "You Can See Everything," stunned Telluride audiences Sunday night with its generous access to the Theranos founder.

item.title: What we expect from the upcoming Apple launch
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: While Apple's first foldable iPhone Ultra will headline the September 9 launch, we're also expecting news about AirPods and HomePods.

item.title: Phil Schiller’s App Store exit reportedly driven by wariness over future plans
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: Schiller reportedly had reservations about new CEO John Ternus' goal of bringing in more recurring revenue from the App Store.
